k8s.replicaset.non_root.description: A ReplicaSet Pod template is flagged when a Linux container does not have effective runAsNonRoot true or explicitly uses UID zero. This matters because the process can start with root identity.
k8s.replicaset.non_root.pass_when: On Linux, every regular, init, and ephemeral container has effective runAsNonRoot=true (container setting overrides the Pod setting) and no effective runAsUser=0.
k8s.replicaset.non_root.fail_when: On Linux, a regular, init, or ephemeral container has effective runAsNonRoot=false or effective runAsUser=0.
k8s.replicaset.non_root.not_applicable_when: The Pod template declares Windows OS, so the Linux non-root check is inapplicable. On a positively identified provider- or control-plane-managed object, the registration wrapper changes an underlying FAIL, MANUAL, UNKNOWN, or DENIED to NOT_APPLICABLE; an underlying PASS remains PASS.

k8s.service.review_public_type.description: A Service is flagged when it declares externalIPs or an unrestricted NodePort or LoadBalancer type. This can publish the workload through node ports, load balancers, or external address routing; internal load balancer annotations or restricted source ranges suppress the type-based finding.
k8s.service.review_public_type.pass_when: There are no externalIPs and the Service type is internal or its LoadBalancer declaration is treated as restricted.
k8s.service.review_public_type.fail_when: There are externalIPs, or an unrestricted NodePort or LoadBalancer declaration.
